ENCOUNTER NOTE
Date: 2022-01-15
Provider: Dr. James Wilson, MD
Department: Emergency Medicine
Visit Type: ed

CHIEF COMPLAINT:
Fever, sore throat, and difficulty breathing

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS:
The patient returns to the emergency department two years after his prior presentation for drain cleaner ingestion. He is brought by his parents due to a 6-hour history of fever, sore throat, and difficulty breathing. The parents report that the child has been drooling and seems to prefer sitting upright. They also note that his voice sounds muffled.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY:
Active Problem List:
- Peptic esophageal stricture (diagnosed 2020-01-15)

The child has received his vaccinations according to the local schedule, but the parents are unsure if he has received the Haemophilus influenzae type b vaccine.

ALLERGIES:
NKDA

FAMILY HISTORY:
- Maternal grandfather with hypertension
- Paternal grandmother with type 2 diabetes mellitus

SOCIAL HISTORY:
Smoking: Never. Alcohol: Never. Occupation: Preschool student.

VITAL SIGNS:
, has a temperature of 39.2°C (102.5°F), a heart rate of 130 beats per minute, and a respiratory rate of 40 breaths per minute.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION:
On examination, the child appears anxious
He is sitting upright, leaning forward, and drooling. His voice is muffled, and inspiratory stridor is noted. The oropharynx is erythematous without exudates, and attempts to examine the throat further cause the child to become agitated.

IMAGING:
Lateral neck radiography shows a swollen epiglottis with a "thumbprint" sign.

ENCOUNTER NOTE
Date: 2020-01-15
Provider: Dr. Priya Sharma, MD
Department: Emergency Medicine
Visit Type: ed

CHIEF COMPLAINT:
Drinking from a bottle of drain cleaner approximately 30 minutes ago

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS:
He is brought to the emergency department by his parents after they witnessed him drinking from a bottle of drain cleaner approximately 30 minutes ago. The parents report that he immediately began crying and drooling and now refuses to eat or drink.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY:
His past medical history is unremarkable, and his immunizations are up to date.

ALLERGIES:
NKDA

FAMILY HISTORY:
- Maternal grandfather with hypertension
- Paternal grandmother with type 2 diabetes mellitus

SOCIAL HISTORY:
Smoking: Never. Alcohol: Never. Occupation: Preschool student.

VITAL SIGNS:
His vital signs are as follows: temperature 37.2°C (99°F), pulse 130/min, respirations 30/min, and blood pressure 95/60 mmHg.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION:
On examination, the child is anxious but alert. He is drooling and has mild stridor at rest. His oropharynx is erythematous without discrete lesions, and there is no crepitus on palpation of the neck. There is no abdominal tenderness, and bowel sounds are normal. The remainder of the physical examination is unremarkable.
